prompt:
Normalize the single contact record in the user's note. Use only its labeled value lines, not surrounding text, signatures, email domains or suffix-based guesses. Labels vary and lines may be shuffled; separators include colon, equals and tab. Return only a bare JSON object with exactly name, phone, email, company, country, each a string or null.

Trim values and collapse whitespace runs. Absent, empty or placeholder values (-, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD, any case) are null. Never infer missing values except for the country fallback below.

Assign email by @ and phone by at least seven digits with only digits, spaces or + - ( ) . / after removing a leading tel: and an extension (ext. 12, ext 12, x12, #12, extension 12). These tests override labels. Swap name and company if the name value ends in a listed legal suffix and the company value does not. Explicit country comes only from its own line.

Name: reorder Last, First at the first comma; drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof (optional dot, any case); uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Keep Unicode letters and diacritics without transliteration; comparison uses NFC.

Company: remove a trailing suffix and optional preceding comma, case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word. Email: strip mailto: and surrounding angle brackets, then lowercase the whole address.

Country: uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish and German names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, all case-insensitively, and common aliases including UK/Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA/U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR, Czech Republic → CZ.

Phone: remove tel: and extensions. A prefix of + or 00, ignoring an opening parenthesis, marks an international number. Replace initial 00 with +, delete (0), strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, and keep its calling code even if the country line disagrees. Only when country is absent, empty or a placeholder, infer it from an international phone's uniquely assigned calling code; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. For national numbers, strip formatting, remove one leading trunk 0, and prepend + and the normalized country's calling code; without a country, return null for phone. Non-null phones are E.164: + followed only by calling code and national significant number digits.
